newsitem.title: KENYA: Uganda says coffee disease widespread, devastating.
newsitem.headline: Uganda says coffee disease widespread, devastating.

text.p: Findings of an investigation ordered by the Uganda Coffee Development Authority (UCDA) show that coffee wilt disease (tracheomycosis) is widespread and devastating in southwestern districts that border Zaire.
UCDA said in its 1995/96 final quarter report that the highest occurrence of the disease was in the districts of Bundibugyo, Kasese and Rukungiri that border eastern Zaire.
"The coffee disease did affect some plantations resulting in uprooting of infected trees," said the report on Tuesday.

UCDA also confirmed reports that damage caused by hail in some key growing districts as well as disease were partly responsible for a downward forecast in coffee exports in 1996/97 to 3.6 million 60 kg bags from a record 4.15 million bags in 1995/96.
Tracheomycosis causes rotting of the root system, degeneration of the plant, fading of colour in the leaves and wilting, leading to the death of a tree in 4-7 days.
UCDA added that in the centrally-located districts of Mukono, Kiboga and Mubende, where the disease had been reported, it was observed to be localised but devastating.
UCDA said the task force recommended total destruction of infected coffee trees.
In addition, it recommended restriction of movement of coffee planting materials, coffee cherries and coffee husks from district to district.
It also called for greater sensitisation to the disease by all stakeholders in the coffee sub-sector, as well as improved general sanitation and crop husbandry practices.

The task force called for a crop quarantine on Bundibugyo and other districts in which the disease had been sighted and other areas that may fall victim. It called for epidemiological studies of coffee wilt disease and screening for resistance.
"The disease is said to have originated from eastern Zaire where it has a long history of devastating coffee fields. It was observed only affecting the robusta variety," UCDA said.
Around 90 percent of Ugandan exports are robustas.
UCDA said an economic evaluation of the disease was undertaken in Bundibugyo based on a sample of 72 randomly selected farmers in seven sub-counties of Bwamba district.
"Sixty percent of the robusta trees in Bundibygyo was affected by the coffee wilt disease," UCDA said.
UCDA said it estimated total coffee lost from a sample of 82.2 acres was about 9,919 kg of clean coffee per year (equivalent to $9,900 per year) from a total of 18,369 trees.
"The implied economic losses are enormous," UCDA said.
